u0: Normal progress: no fall from the preceding step is still waiting to be recovered, and the main goal remains to reach the exit with the box in your hands. The box may be carried, or it may have been set down after a recovery and need to be picked up again before the exit. A new fall changes the requirement immediately: the box must be held again on the very next step.
u1: A box fall has just occurred before the exit, so an immediate recovery is required. On the very next step the box must be in your hands; doing so returns you to normal progress, while doing so at the exit would complete the task. If that next step leaves you without the box, the missed pickup is a permanent failure.
u2: The exit has been reached, but the box is not in your hands, so the task is not complete. The remaining objective is to get the box into your possession; holding it on a later step with no simultaneous fall finishes the task. Until then progress waits, and a fall imposes the requirement that the box be held again on the immediately following step.
u3: The exit has been reached and the box is in your hands, with every earlier fall having been recovered immediately. All requirements are satisfied, so the task is complete and no further objective remains.
u4: The exit has already been reached without the box, and a fall has just occurred; the box is not in your hands, so a pickup is immediately due. You must be holding it on the very next step to finish; if not, the missed pickup is a permanent failure. This pending recovery cannot return to ordinary progress.
u5: The exit has already been reached, and a fall has just occurred while the box is in your hands, so the next step must still be a carrying step. Holding the box then completes the task; failing to hold it is a permanent failure.
u6: A required fall recovery was missed: after the box fell, it was not back in your hands on the immediately following step. This breaks a mandatory requirement permanently, so successful completion is no longer possible even if the box is later picked up or the exit is reached.
